evidence.field: 字形; 說文; 形義通解; historical examples
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 歡 as 从欠、雚聲 and gives the basic sense as happiness or joy. It reports a received 《洛誥》 citation, then examples for being on friendly terms in 《史記·田敬仲完世家》, a lover addressed as 歡 in 《子夜歌》, and a later ‘vigorously’ sense in a Tang 王涯 poem. These are source-reported examples; the entry does not date each textual witness.
evidence.kind: character-dictionary account and cited historical examples
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Research of Unearthed Texts and Ancient Characters, 雷燮仁
evidence.text: The commentary reports readings of the 洛誥 phrase 公功肅將祗歡 as involving either joy or alternative parses, including readings of 歡 as 勸 and proposals involving 灌. The author favors parsing it as 勸功. The transmitted phrase therefore cannot securely establish an early ordinary ‘joy’ sense on its own.
evidence.title: 雷燮仁：《尚書集注試解·洛誥》（徵求意見稿）

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry classifies 欢 as a variant of 歡 and cites 《宋元以來俗字譜》 examples from 目連記 and 金瓶梅, along with 字學三正’s statement that 歡 is popularly written 欢. It also links 欢 to 歎 as a separate variant, with a distinct tàn reading. The citations establish premodern variant use but do not date individual occurrences or their manuscript witnesses.
evidence.title: [A02065] 歡 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry records 欢 with huān as a variant of 歡 and tàn as a variant of 歎. It gives the traditional analysis of 歡 as 喜樂也、從欠，雚聲 and reports examples of 欢 in 目連記 and 金瓶梅. Thus the simplified-looking glyph can represent distinct graph histories/readings in different contexts.
evidence.title: [A02065-001] 欢 (歡) - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A02052 說文釋形 and meanings
evidence.text: The entry reports Shuowen’s analysis of 欠 as 张口气悟也, depicting breath rising above a person. It records meanings including breathing/yawning, moving the body slightly, and deficiency. It does not say 欠 depicts laughter in 歡; a laughter-related interpretation for the component remains inferential.
evidence.title: [A02052] 欠 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: Shuowen.org, Shuowen Jiezi and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.field: 雚 entry; received gloss and Duan correction
evidence.text: The received Shuowen entry glosses 雚 as 小爵, analyzes it as 从雈、吅聲, and cites 詩曰雚鳴于垤. Duan Yucai emends the gloss to 雚爵/雀 and identifies the bird with 鸛, noting that received 詩 text has 鸛 and that 雚 is a textual variant. The bird identification and precise referent are therefore textually disputed; the source does not recover an independently certain spoken name for the bird.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and editorial correction
evidence.title: 說文解字「雚」

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, official Old Chinese reconstruction table, version 1.1
evidence.field: radical/stroke table page 70; 歡 row; local cross-check sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 1350
evidence.text: The official table gives 歡 huān, Middle Chinese xwan (x- + -wan A), Old Chinese *qʷʰˤar, gloss ‘rejoice; joyous.’ The exact local TSV row agrees. These are Baxter–Sagart system notations; they should not be merged with reconstructions from other systems.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, official Old Chinese reconstruction table, version 1.1
evidence.field: radical/stroke table page 150; 雚 row; local cross-check sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv row 1144
evidence.text: The table gives 雚 guàn, Middle Chinese kwanH (k- + -wan C), Old Chinese *C.qʷˤar-s, gloss ‘heron.’ The local TSV row agrees exactly. Comparing these readings within Baxter–Sagart shows a close onset and rhyme between 雚 and 歡, consistent with 雚 serving phonetically in 歡, although their prefixes and suffixes differ. This supports a sound-component analysis, not a claim that a bird name was borrowed as a whole graph or word.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (13 September 2014)

gaps: No image candidate met both identity and provenance requirements: Commons searches surfaced unrelated glyphs, and Xiaoxuetang’s official query interface did not expose a specific 歡 record or supplied direct glyph URL in the rendered access available. No image is proposed.

The consulted CUHK entry shows seal and bamboo/silk examples but no oracle-bone or bronze examples in its displayed record; this is a database display gap, not proof that the graph did not exist earlier.

The earliest secure date for the 歡 graph remains unresolved. The 洛誥 passage is early textual material but its phrase is disputed, including readings as 勸 or 灌, so it cannot securely establish an early ordinary ‘joy’ sense.

The Taiwan variant dictionary documents 欢 in named premodern works but the inspected entry does not provide dated occurrences or manuscript-witness dates. It also records 欢 as a variant of 歎 in a separate reading context, so graph identity alone does not establish the intended word.
The laughter-related interpretation of 欠 is not directly established by the inspected sources. Shuowen describes open-mouth breathing/yawning; any laughter nuance in 歡 is an interpretation.

The exact referent/name and pronunciation of 雚 as a bird are not fully settled: received Shuowen has 小爵, while Duan Yucai emends it and identifies 鸛. The Baxter–Sagart table independently lists 雚 as guàn, MC kwanH, OC *C.qʷˤar-s, ‘heron,’ but this does not prove a whole-word bird-name loan. It does independently support the phonetic comparison of 雚 within 歡.

The Baxter–Sagart local rows were verified against the inspected official university-hosted table. The different Zhengzhang reconstruction in the dossier is a separate system and is not reconciled or silently substituted here.
No evidence was found for borrowing the whole graph 歡 as another word. The supported received analysis is phonosemantic: 欠 as semantic component and 雚 as sound component.

limitations.text: No usable, attributable historical 歡 glyph image was verified during this run. Commons searches returned unrelated characters, and the Xiaoxuetang interface did not expose a character-specific 歡 glyph image. Consequently no image URL is proposed.
